title: Composite-Boson Ansatz for Fractional Quantum Hall Manifolds of Lattice Bosons at Generic Fillings $ν<1/2$
authors: Umut Can Turhan, A. Levent Subaşı, Rifat Onur Umucalılar
abstract: Hofstadter systems provide a lattice route to fractional quantum Hall physics, but their low-energy manifolds often lack simple wave-function descriptions. Here we present a composite-boson ansatz for a broad family of finite-size lattice-split Laughlin-quasihole manifolds in the low-flux Hofstadter--Bose--Hubbard model on a torus at generic fillings \(ν<1/2\). Attaching two vortices to each boson yields reduced-flux orbitals from which we construct a many-body trial basis. Its translation-resolved rank reproduces the expected low-energy-manifold dimension and provides a composite-boson interpretation of the established quasihole counting previously inferred from generalized exclusion rules and thin-torus arguments. For smaller systems, diagonalization within the lowest-band-projected ansatz span closely reproduces the exact projected spectrum, while variational Monte Carlo extends the rank and energetic analysis to larger systems for which explicit subspace construction becomes costly. To probe the fractional quantum Hall character of these manifolds, we calculate their many-body Chern-numbers and show that localized added-flux excitations exhibit quasihole-like behavior, with fractional density depletion and an Aharonov--Bohm-free braiding phase that both track the effective filling. Together, these results establish a microscopic composite-boson framework for organizing a broad family of sub-half-filled fractional quantum Hall manifolds of lattice bosons.
summary: This paper develops and validates a composite-boson ansatz to microscopically describe the low-energy states of lattice bosons exhibiting fractional quantum Hall physics at fillings less than 1/2. By calculating key topological invariants like Chern numbers and analyzing quasihole braiding, the authors establish a robust theoretical framework that successfully maps complex FQH behavior onto a manageable bosonic Hilbert space.
main_problem: The research aims to develop a microscopic composite-boson framework to describe the low-energy manifolds of fractional quantum Hall (FQH) systems realized on lattices at generic fillings $\nu < 1/2$. This moves beyond simple counting rules by providing a structured wave function ansatz.
main_result: The proposed composite-boson ansatz successfully organizes the low-energy space, reproducing the expected manifold degeneracy and exhibiting characteristic fractional topological responses like quasihole density depletion and specific braiding phases.
method: The study employs constructing a many-body trial basis using a composite-boson ansatz derived from reduced-flux orbitals. Calculations involve variational Monte Carlo (VMC) for large systems and direct diagonalization for small ones to probe the spectrum and topological invariants.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by interacting bosons on a square lattice governed by the Hofstadter–Bose–Hubbard (HBH) model, studied on a torus geometry. The physics mimics FQH states at sub-half fillings ($\nu < 1/2$).
key_observables: Many-body Chern number ($C_{	ext{MB}}$), quasihole charge diagnostic $Q(R)$, Aharonov–Bohm braiding phase $\theta_B$, and the low-energy manifold dimension (rank).
important_parameters: Generic fillings $\nu < 1/2$; lattice parameters related to the Hofstadter model; reduced flux quantum numbers.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the system's low-energy physics can be captured by a composite-boson wave function ansatz built from reduced-flux orbitals. VMC is used as a controlled numerical summation method for large systems.
figures_summary: Figures compare exact and ansatz spectra, show density depletion plateaus matching $\nu_{	ext{eff}}$, and illustrate the mean Berry phase ($\theta_B$) matching $2\nu_{	ext{eff}}$ for quasihole braiding.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem by noting the limitations of simple descriptions for FQH manifolds on lattices. It then details the composite-boson ansatz construction, validates it by reproducing known degeneracies and topological invariants (Chern numbers, braiding phases), and finally applies advanced numerical techniques like VMC to confirm results for larger systems.
why_interesting: This work bridges concepts from strongly correlated electron physics (FQH states) with lattice models using bosonic descriptions. The explicit construction of a composite-boson basis provides a powerful theoretical tool for understanding topological order in condensed matter systems, which is relevant to AMO platforms simulating these interactions.
